[Architecture overview](../export-design.html).

This topic covers obtaining and preparing both code-list and registry catalogues.

## ObServe code-list catalogue — How do we obtain or build it? {#observe-code-list-catalogue-how-do-we-obtain-or-build-it}

Each country may manage its own referential independently of the IRD.

**Level 1 — catalogue extracted from the source database**

Use SQL queries to extract the referential from the ObServe database used for the export.

R code builds the catalogue using the existing `form.references` APIs.

This level requires neither a public catalogue nor synchronization with the IRD.

**Level 2 — public, versioned catalogue**

Use a public, versioned ObServe catalogue.

The source database must then be synchronized with the selected catalogue using ObServe's referential synchronization.

This prerequisite applies to PostgreSQL and H2. The exporter does not perform synchronization itself.

Technical IDs (`topiaId`) remain stable within the selected referential across databases and catalogue versions.

Select an explicit catalogue version compatible with ObServe 10.0, record it, and reuse its snapshot throughout the export.

**Rules shared by both levels**

Unused entries are disabled through their `status` field, never removed from the catalogue.

Disabled entries remain resolvable for historical observations; their status alone does not invalidate an export.

Report any referenced ID missing from that catalogue as an inconsistency; do not silently substitute another entry.

People and vessels belong to the separate registry catalogue and retain its access controls.

## Reference catalogues

Each gear has a catalogue configuration under `inst/10.0/<gear>/references.yaml`, shared by its ROS form versions.

LL includes `common` and `ll_*` tables; PS includes `common` and `ps_*` tables.

* `code_lists`: reference codes such as species, countries, harbours and activity types.
* `registries`: people, vessels and other registry tables, including `common.person` and `common.vessel`.

The lookup definitions come from the frozen `20261112T184113Z` catalogue snapshot.

Set `OBSERVE_CODE_LISTS_URL` and `OBSERVE_REGISTRIES_URL` to external catalogue directories or HTTPS base URLs.

Only definitions are packaged; catalogue data and persistent caches remain outside the package.

[Download the ObServe 10.0 LL catalogue configuration](../../10.0/ll/references.yaml).

[Download the ObServe 10.0 PS catalogue configuration](../../10.0/ps/references.yaml).

This separates code correspondence from matching people and vessels to the corresponding ROS registry records.

An ObServe person may be an observer, captain or data-entry operator; its role determines the target mapping.

Extracted foreign-key values remain ObServe IDs. Catalogue lookups use the source column name `topiaid`.

Use `ros.form.references` for target ROS reference values and lookup policies.

Existing catalogue aliases and mapping-owned correspondences are distinct; both are covered by the shared design.

Some mappings need additional reference tables reached through another reference, such as a harbour's country.

Each sheet review must identify those dependencies so reference preparation can include them.

## Shared mapping design

Code lists and registries use the same generic lookup and mapping mechanisms.

Read the [mapping design](mapping-design.html) for direct lookups, aliases, business rules and their shared context.

Configured lookups may use exact matching or normalized-name matching; ambiguous results remain explicit.

The design also records coverage of encountered values, delivery scopes, result handling and version traceability.

Concrete mappings are specified in [04 — Code lists](../04-references-code-lists/index.html)
and [05 — Registries](../05-references-registries/index.html).
